explanation: It came from a gland of murex sea snails, and thousands were needed to dye a single robe. The Phoenician city of Tyre, in present-day Lebanon, was famous for it.

claims.text: Tyrian purple was made from a secretion of murex sea snails.
Tyrian purple was worn by Roman and Byzantine emperors as a mark of status.
Tyrian purple was not made from beetles, berries or lichen.
Thousands of murex snails were needed to dye a single garment with Tyrian purple.
The Phoenician city of Tyre, in present-day Lebanon, was famous for producing Tyrian purple.
